integrity: The Palm identity is proved by an exact deletion bijection, and the stochastic comparison by deleting a distinguished chord from a uniform matching. The simple-chord variance is derived directly. The crossing variance is an established exact formula from the cited primary literature and is independently replayed by exhaustive finite enumeration.
scientific_limitations: The marked-deletion identity uses simple chords; positive-length chords can create crossings and require an additional term.
The result is a mixed-moment and monotone-transform statement and does not assert full negative association.
Older generating-function treatments of chord diagrams may encode the same mixed first moment implicitly.
title: A marked simple chord gives an exact crossing Palm law
